C05-M01-L07-F1.title: An isolated practice lab and the paths it blocks
C05-M01-L07-F1.caption: Targets live on loopback or a host-only network inside the host; no adapter connects the lab to the physical LAN or the internet.
C05-M01-L07-F1.alt: Graph. Host computer (your own machine, patched, non-admin user) connects to Loopback lab target (app.py on 127.0.0.1:8099) and to Host-only network (e.g. 192.168.56.0/24, no route out). The host-only network connects Tester VM (tools, scope-checked), which connects to Target VM (snapshot before every session). Dashed arrows labelled blocked: no bridged or NAT adapter run from the Host-only network to Physical LAN (home, office, campus) and to Internet (third-party systems), both shown in red as out of scope.

C05-M01-L07-F1.note: Isolation is a property of the whole topology: one bridged adapter joins the lab to someone else's network.

C05-M01-L07-F2.title: How the kit's tools enforce scope before acting
C05-M01-L07-F2.caption: Each tool checks the host against an allowlist, then checks the target is up, and only then runs its read-only checks.
C05-M01-L07-F2.alt: Decision graph. Tool invoked (enumerate.py / retest.py --host X) leads to decision Host in ALLOWED_HOSTS? (127.0.0.1 or localhost only). No leads to REFUSED, exit 2 (no packet sent). Yes leads to decision Target reachable on loopback? (TCP connect, 1-second timeout). No leads to Stop, exit 1 (start target/app.py first). Yes leads to Run safe checks (read-only, evidence to data/).
C05-M01-L07-F2.note: Scope is checked before reachability, so an out-of-scope host never receives even a connection attempt.
